trust_decision.summary: Whether a repo's configured commit/tag carries a signature from an allowed signer is decided by Repo.check_signature (git verify-commit/verify-tag) in ReposCheckSignatures, which at the pinned commit runs only after every repo has been checked out and its kas include files merged into the config, and git checkout resolves the ref differently from verify-commit.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'late signature validation'. That leads to the ReposCheckSignatures step and its place after ReposCheckout in the Macro step list (kas/libcmds.py:85-86).

fix_sites.entry_point: every Macro-based CLI command (kas checkout/build/shell/for-all-repos/dump/lock/diff/clean) via SetupReposStep in the include-resolution repo_setup_loop
same CLI commands via the ReposCheckout setup step
same CLI commands; the step is removed and its logic moved to SignatureValidator in kas/repos.py (fix.diff:137-178)
GitRepo.checkout_cmd, reached from Repo.checkout (kas/repos.py:558) on every checkout of a 40/64-hex desired_ref

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: kas/repos.py:767-768 (fix.diff:12-17): GitRepo.checkout_cmd builds 'git checkout <sha>'. A local branch named like the SHA is checked out instead of the commit object that verify-commit checked (kas/repos.py:750-751). This is a parser differential on the identity of the verified item, and it sits in a different file and layer from the step-ordering bug.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about ordering ('late validation'), so moving the check before checkout looks complete. The git-level command builder looks like an unrelated ref-resolution detail, because verify-commit and checkout are handed the same string.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Unsigned repos (no allowed_signers) and local repos without url/ref must keep checking out with no key handler present. Repos on a branch without a pinned commit must still verify origin/<branch>. Checkout by a branch name or a short ref must not be forced into '^{commit}'. An over-broad fix (verify every repo, or rewrite every ref) breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: tag (verify-tag <tag>; checkout of the resolved tag SHA)
branch without commit (verify-commit on resolved origin/<branch> SHA)
repos reached in the include loop vs repos in the final config

O7_producer.where: kas/includehandler.py:318-334 merges kas files read from repos checked out in kas/libcmds.py:612-616. The merged config feeds Repo.factory, which sets signed/allowed_signers (kas/repos.py:310-314) and get_signers_config, and so decides what is verified and against which keys.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: When the repo is dirty, checkout is skipped, but verification still checks the configured commit object and never the HEAD/working tree that is actually used.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Dirty-repo skip is a deliberate developer workflow that kas warns about, so it looks like local user state, not repository manipulation.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as checkout_cmd fix; different function from the libcmds step

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Signer public keys are read from another repo's working tree (signers.<id>.repo/path). That key repo is not required to be signed, and keys are imported before it may have been verified or checked out.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The user's config picks which repo holds the trust anchor, so this can be argued as configuration rather than a validation-order bug.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another file (kas/keyhandler.py), two hops from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: prepare_patches_cmd runs 'git checkout -B patched-<ref>' from the configured ref. A variant that checks out self.commit directly would repeat the sha-like-branch differential.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a second checkout command builder in the same class, built from the same commit/tag/branch fields.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: contains_refspec_cmd / get_commit_cmd (kas/repos.py:791-793) resolve the bare commit string. A planted resolve-then-checkout using a ref instead of '^{commit}' is a natural HOW-type sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Several helpers resolve the same user string with different git plumbing commands, so an inconsistency is easy to write.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A plugin step that reads files from repos (e.g. lockfile generation or for-all-repos commands) before the per-repo validation call.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Plugins compose the Macro steps with custom --skip lists, so a maintainer could add a step that reads repo content early.

O9_family: CWE-347 improper signature verification / TOCTOU between verification and use of VCS content (A04 insecure design)

O10_build.toolchain: python3 + pip (kas package), git, gpg (python-gnupg), ssh-keygen
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_signature_verify.py; the gpg tests are marked online (keyserver recv_keys, upstream repo clone), test_signed_ssh_key builds a local repo and runs offline (tests/test_signature_verify.py:103-140)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Move ReposCheckSignatures before ReposCheckout in the Macro list (kas/libcmds.py:85-86). This misses the include loop checkout (kas/libcmds.py:612-616) and the sha-like ref differential in checkout_cmd.

out_of_scope_notes: The published regex '^[0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64}$' (fix.diff:15) has an alternation-precedence flaw: it anchors only one side of each alternative.

After the fix, validation lives inside repos_checkout/repo_setup_loop, so '-k' (kas/libkas.py:709-715) or '--skip repos_checkout' also skips validation. At the pinned commit, repos_check_signatures was a separately skippable step (kas/libkas.py:650-657).
